newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto demands inquiry into Pakistan wheat crisis.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto demands inquiry into Pakistan wheat crisis.

text.p: Pakistani opposition leader Benazir Bhutto called on Sunday for an inquiry into a flour shortage that has sparked unrest in several cities.

"We demand a judicial commission to inquire into the causes of the flour crisis," the former prime minister told Reuters after distributing free flour to the poor on Baba Bhit island, off the coast of Karachi.
She handed out 400 bags of flour to islanders in an operation organised by her Pakistan People's Party.
"I am not here to blame anyone for the crisis. I am not going to say (Prime Minister) Nawaz Sharif or (President) Farooq Leghari was responsible," Bhutto said.
She said the proposed commission should identify those responsible and suggest ways to avoid further shortages.
Bhutto said there had been no wheat shortage under her three-year government, dismissed by Leghari on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Flour shortages have hit several cities in recent weeks. Karachi, previously spared, ran short ahead of the Moslem feast of Eid al-Adha, which began on Thursday.

Sharif's government blames the previous caretaker administration for failing to arrange timely wheat imports, but flour mill-owners fault the government for a ban on the movement of wheat within Pakistan and price controls.

The Pakistan Flour Mills Association said on Saturday the flour crisis was almost over in Karachi, where fresh supplies were trucked in from the interior of Sindh province, of which the southern port city is the capital.
Pakistan imported 1.8 million tonnes of wheat in July-March 1996/97 compared to 1.5 million in the year-ago period.
